title: Trivial minimum cut on the max-flow entry's random dense networks
statement: Model: vertices 0..n-1, s = 0, t = n-1, M = the other m = n-2 vertices; every ordered pair (u, v), u != v, is an edge independently with probability 1/2 and capacity uniform on {1..100} (the generator generate_scaling of pairs/max-flow-edmonds-karp-vs-dinic with ideal random bits). Let C be the event that c(S', M - S') > 100 min(|S'|, |M - S'|) for every nonempty proper subset S' of M. (a) Deterministic: on every network with non-negative integer capacities, a_v = c(s, v) and b_v = c(v, t) in [0, 100], that satisfies C, every s-t cut other than ({s}, V - {s}) and (V - {t}, {t}) has capacity > min(c_out(s), c_in(t)); hence the maximum flow value is min(c_out(s), c_in(t)), the minimum cuts are exactly the trivial cuts attaining it, and both implementations of the entry return it. (b) P(not C) <= B(n) = sum_{j=1}^{m-1} C(m, j) inf_{theta>0} e^{100 min(j, m-j) theta} phi(theta)^{j(m-j)}, phi(theta) = 1/2 + (1/200) sum_{c=1}^{100} e^{-theta c}; B(n) -> 0; B(n) <= 5.474e-5 at n = 40 and <= 4.876e-101 at n = 400; B(n) < 1 for every n >= 22, B(n) < 5.48e-5 and B(n) <= 1/n for every n >= 40, and B(n) < 7.6e-6 for every n >= 202 (computed in decimal arithmetic with certified rounding for 22 <= n <= 201, by a written tail bound above); for n <= 21 the computed bound is >= 1. (c) With Delta = c_out(s) - c_in(t): P(Delta = 0) <= sqrt(2/m) + e^{-0.1225 m} and P(Delta < 0) = P(Delta > 0); each trivial cut is the only minimum cut with probability between 1/2 - (sqrt(2/m) + e^{-0.1225 m})/2 - P(not C) and 1/2, so the winning trivial cut is asymptotically a fair coin.

bases: Karp 1979 (Tenth International Symposium on Mathematical Programming; not accessible), credited by Karp, Motwani and Nisan (1988 report, p. 5; journal text) with the almost-sure trivial minimum cut on complete graphs with i.i.d. capacities

Grimmett–Welsh 1982 (Stochastics 7(3), doi:10.1080/17442508208833219), Theorem 3.3: first-order limits of the maximum-flow value on complete graphs (undirected, or one orientation per pair); read, no trivial-cut statement
Grimmett–Suen 1982 (Stochastics 8(2), doi:10.1080/17442508208833234), Theorems 1-2: first-order limits of the maximum-flow value (one orientation per pair); read, no trivial-cut statement
provenance.pending_note: Probably our own result: the sources read (Grimmett-Welsh 1982, Sections 1 and 3; Grimmett-Suen 1982 in full; Karp-Motwani-Nisan, journal text and parts of the 1988 report) do not state it for this model. Grimmett-Welsh and Grimmett-Suen give results on the flow value only (limits for undirected or one-orientation models, bounds on its mean); Karp-Motwani-Nisan's own theorems do not apply (multiple-source theorem: undirected graphs with unit capacities; single-source theorem: given source and sink capacities). Karp 1979 (Tenth International Symposium on Mathematical Programming), which Karp, Motwani and Nisan credit with the trivial minimum cut, could not be read; whether it states the result for this model (capacity 0 with probability 1/2, both orientations of every pair, random source and sink capacities) is open.
